_comment: Copy this file to config.json and edit the values. All steps run unattended from these values. Do NOT commit config.json (it contains passwords).

DHCP._comment: false skips step 5 AND the DHCP role install in step 2 - use it when something else on the network already serves DHCP.

SQL._comment: InstallFolder is both where the ISO is looked for and where SQL installs. Step 8 uses InstallFolder\SQL_Server_Install.iso, else any .iso over 300 MB in that folder (so a hand-copied ISO works under any name), else downloads DownloadUrl. Leave DownloadUrl empty to install strictly from a staged ISO.

Staging._comment: Step 6b - robocopy folders off removable media onto the server disk BEFORE SQL installs. SourceRoot is the USB key, DestinationRoot the internal disk; each Folders entry is copied SourceRoot\<name> -> DestinationRoot\<name>. Empty Folders = every top-level folder on the media. ExcludeFiles takes robocopy /XF patterns.

FileShares._comment: Step 7, second half: create each Path, set its NTFS rights, and share it as ShareName over SMB. Leave ShareName empty to create the folder without sharing. Access lists take bare group names (GG_Technicien) resolved against the real domain NetBIOS name, or fully qualified DOMAIN\Group; well-known groups such as Domain Admins are auto-corrected to their real, possibly localized name. FullAccess=FullControl, ChangeAccess=Modify, ReadAccess=ReadAndExecute. ApplyNtfs true rebuilds the folder ACL from these lists (inheritance broken; SYSTEM and Administrators always kept) - set false to write share permissions only. The GG_* department groups are created in step 6. Copying is done by the Staging section above.

Database._comment: Order: restore each Restores[].BakFile (found in BackupFolder) as DatabaseName relocating its files to DataFolder; set Mixed-Mode and restart SQL; run CustomSqlScript verbatim (inline T-SQL or a .sql path, GO separators supported); create SqlLogin only if Create is true; finally grant SqlLogin.Name db_owner on DbOwnerOf. The db_owner grant runs even when Create is false, so a login created by CustomSqlScript still gets ownership. A bare CREATE LOGIN in CustomSqlScript is not re-runnable - guard it with IF NOT EXISTS if step 9 may run twice.
